audit.whatIsWrong: The seven 'why' rows are shifted one stage late from Levels 4-5 onward: whys[3] (Levels 4-5) describes Riftwalk blinking over Pillar, and whys[4] (Level 6) describes the Rod of Ages timing.
audit.why: Riftwalk unlocks at level 6. A Levels 4-5 row that tells you to blink over Pillar of Ice is describing a button you do not have, and it is exactly the kind of line that gets a Kassadin killed at level 5 waiting for an escape that will not cast. Realigning them also puts the Rod of Ages spike back on the First-item stage where the spikes array already places it.
audit.corrected: Levels 4-5 is the survival grind (Catalyst, Nether Blade refunds, still losing every auto trade). Level 6 is where Riftwalk arrives and the Pillar stops being a cage.

audit.why: Spike timings are right — level 6 for Riftwalk, Catalyst/Rod of Ages as the stabiliser, two items for the inversion. Trundle's own spike, Subjugate at 6, is named. I only attached the missing number to it (120/100/80s) rather than moving any timing.

Pillar of Ice is not a gap-closer and Trundle does not have one. Riot's text: 'Trundle creates an ice pillar at target location, becoming impassable terrain and slowing all nearby enemy units' — cast range 1000, cooldown 21/19.5/18/16.5/15. It closes YOUR exit, it does not move him. That distinction changes the whole spacing plan: you are not dodging a dash, you are refusing to stand anywhere a 1000-range wall can seal. Calling it a gap-closer makes a Kassadin watch the wrong thing.
audit.corrected: Trundle has no gap-closer at all. Pillar of Ice is a 1000-range piece of impassable terrain on a 21s cooldown at rank 1 — it cuts your retreat, it does not bring him to you.

audit.whatIsWrong: Subjugate is named as 'the clock this lane runs on' in four places without its cooldown, and the resist-steal is described as 'your resists' without saying it takes armour AND magic resist and doubles.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Trundle immediately steals a percent of his target's Health, Armor and Magic Resistance. Over the next 4 seconds the amount stolen is doubled', cooldown 120/100/80, range 650. Two things follow that the page never says. First, 120 seconds at rank 1 is an enormous window — if he burns it, you own the next two minutes, which is a concrete green light rather than a vague 'commit on its cooldown'. Second, because it steals magic resist too, buying MR against him is self-defeating; the flagged 'resistances-invalidated' interaction belongs here.
audit.corrected: Subjugate: 120s at rank 1, 650 range. It steals HP, armour and magic resist, and the amount doubles over 4 seconds — so never buy raw MR into him, and treat a spent Subjugate as a two-minute pass.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chomp is described as the thing that beats you but never as an auto-attack reset, and its cooldown is never given.
audit.why: Chomp is 3.5s at every rank, 300 range, and carries the auto-reset flag — 'Trundle bites his opponent, dealing damage, briefly slowing and sapping some of their Attack Damage.' The flagged interaction is that the burst tell is the attack wind-up, not the ability cast: he autos, Chomps instantly, and the two land as one. At 3.5 seconds it is never meaningfully down, which is the real reason 'concede the auto trade' is correct advice — worth stating as a number instead of a mood.
audit.corrected: Chomp is a 3.5s auto-attack reset at 300 range. The wind-up is your cue to back off — by the time you see the bite, both hits have landed.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Force Pulse (its cooldown slashed by every nearby cast)'.
audit.why: Force Pulse is not cooldown-reduced by nearby casts; it is charge-gated by them. Riot: 'Kassadin draws energy from spells cast in his vicinity. Upon charging up, Kassadin can use Force Pulse.' The practical difference matters against Trundle specifically — he is a low-cast-count champion, so in a quiet sidelane your E simply will not be armed, which is a thing to plan around rather than a cooldown you can assume ticks down.
audit.corrected: Force Pulse charges off spells cast near you, from either side. Against a low-cast bruiser like Trundle you often arrive at the fight with it unarmed.

audit.why: 'Add anti-heal early into his sustain' is already in the Itemization row, which is the flagged needs-antiheal interaction (King's Tribute heals off nearby dying units, Frozen Domain increases healing from ALL sources while he stands on it). Nothing to add — the point is covered, so I am not padding it.
57.14% over 7 games. Tiny sample; the page does not quote a figure, so nothing to change. I deliberately did not lean on this number when weighing the level chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Nether Blade's 5x mana refund on champion hits', twice, plus 'Q-silence the counterplay' in breakdown.late.
audit.why: Riot's W text is only 'restores Mana' — no multiplier is published anywhere in the kit file, and the file's needsResearch block is empty on purpose so silence on a number means unknown. Separately, Null Sphere has never silenced in this kit version: it 'interrupts channels' and grants a magic-absorbing shield. Both invented details are removed rather than replaced with different invented ones.
audit.corrected: Nether Blade restores mana; no published multiplier. Null Sphere interrupts channels, it does not silence.

edits.before: Trundle owns the opening. Chomp (Q) bites off your AD and heals him on it, so any auto trade costs you twice, while Frozen Domain (W) gives him a move-speed zone that denies your escape and out-sustains your poke. Do not contest CS with autos — clip minions with the tip of Null Sphere and accept you're behind. His only gap-closer is Pillar (E), so hug open ground and never let him wall you in for a free Chomp-empowered all-in.
edits.after: Trundle owns the opening. Chomp (Q) is a 3.5s auto-attack reset that bites off your AD and heals him, so any auto trade costs you twice, while Frozen Domain (W) is a zone of move speed and increased healing from every source. Do not contest CS with autos — clip minions with the tip of Null Sphere and accept you're behind. He has no gap-closer at all: Pillar (E) is a 1000-range wall that seals your exit, so hug open ground.

edits.before: Level 6 flips your survival. Riftwalk blinks you over his Pillar and out of Chomp range, making his all-in whiff its AD-steal entirely, and Nether Blade's 5x mana refund on champion hits finally lets you cast on cooldown. Once Catalyst into Rod of Ages onlines you out-stall his drain and climb to even. Avoid the straight brawl while Subjugate (R) steals your resistances and heals him — deny the Pillar trap, blink off the all-in, and farm to your 2-item spike.
edits.after: Level 6 flips your survival. Riftwalk blinks you over his Pillar and out of Chomp range, making his all-in whiff its AD-steal entirely, and Nether Blade's mana refund on champion hits finally lets you cast on cooldown. Once Catalyst into Rod of Ages onlines you out-stall his drain and climb to even. Subjugate (R) is 120s at rank 1 and steals HP, armour AND magic resist, doubling over 4s — never buy raw MR, and treat a spent R as a free two minutes.

edits.before: Now the lane inverts for good. His kit is pure AD, so your Void Stone passive's 15% magic reduction does nothing here — but it doesn't need to, because your magic burst shreds his tankiness regardless. Stacked Riftwalk lets you blink in, drop Force Pulse (its cooldown slashed by every nearby cast), and blink out before Chomp-and-Subjugate drain him back to full. He has no ranged threat and no way to pin a blinking assassin, so his only out is splitpushing — answer it by grouping and deleting his carries while he shoves a sidelane alone.
edits.after: Now the lane inverts for good. His kit is pure AD, so your Void Stone passive's magic reduction does nothing here — but it doesn't need to, because your magic burst shreds his tankiness regardless. Stacked Riftwalk lets you blink in, drop Force Pulse (charged by spells cast near you, his included, so it can arrive unarmed), and blink out before Chomp-and-Subjugate drain him full. He has no ranged threat and no dash to pin a blinking assassin, so his only out is splitpushing — group and delete his carries while he shoves alone.

notes: Two structural issues I did NOT touch, both champion-level rather than matchup-level, so they are in questionsForUser. (1) The full-layer level chart gives Trundle all seven stages while the content spikes and whys on the same page say Kassadin inverts the lane at two items — and phases[6].why literally reads 'the monster is awake ... best scaling champion in the lobby' under side 'Trundle'. I left sides and ratings alone because the identical boilerplate why-text appears in matchups where the enemy genuinely does win late (Teemo's audited mirror confirms it there), so the text is not evidence of an intended flip, and 7 games is too small to overrule the chart on its own. (2) The 'diff' label and 'diffRating' disagree in a consistent way across Kassadin: here diff is 'FAV' while breakdown.difficulty reads 'Hard matchup — difficulty 8/10'; on Teemo diff is 'HARD' while difficulty reads 'Even matchup — 5.5/10'. The label looks inverted repo-wide. Also note side/rating edits would breach the ±10% length band by construction ('Trundle' to 'Skill' is -29%), so chart fixes on this champion may need the applier's band to exempt enum fields.
